 iii 67. murderer’s stake] Formerly, the bodies of executed murderers were hanged in chains or irons on
a stake with a projecting arm, known as a gibbet, as a mark of infamy and a measure of dissuasion. See
Zeinab and Kathema (Longman i 171–7, no. 58) 121–38 and note. In the previous stanza, mushrooms
spring from the ground like resurrected corpses; in this one, the flesh of their caps gradually rots from
them as would that of a gibbeted murderer.
 iii 69. Disease and infection had long been associated with bad air; this is the literal meaning of ‘malaria’,
which was a danger to health in early-nineteenth-century Italy (cp. Adonais 457 and note). Some areas
of the country were highly malarial, such as the infamous Maremma described in Mazenghi; see also
the lines from The Cenci quoted in note to iii 58–65. On 26 April 1819, Mary wrote to Maria Gisborne:
